author: Ashley Schuler
title: Great food and summer vibes at Fall River Seafood Festival - NewsBreak
text:
By Ashley Schuler ,
20 hours ago
Calling all local seafood lovers. If you’re fishing for fun way to launch into the summer season, the Fall River Seafood Festival will have you hooked.
“An unforgettable afternoon of flavor, music, and coastal celebration,” is headed to the city waterfront Saturday, May 23, from 2 to 6 p.m. as the Seafood Festival makes a splash along Heritage State Park and the Fall River Carousel.
The event promises to be the “reel” deal for fresh, locally sourced seafood, creative coastal bites and brews from area establishments, and endless summer vibes.
Here's what to know before you go:
What restaurants will be at the Fall River Seafood Festival? The event will have food trucks that include:
Blount Fine Foods Gnarly Vine Farms Ms. Emily's Fresh Seafood Hometown Poke Hot Potato Green Jar Cocina Del's Lemonade Jerry's Concessions Enjoy seafood tastings from some of the best local restaurants at Kyler’s Seafood Hall, presented by Kyler’s Catch of New Bedford.
Inside the seafood hall, you'll find offerings from these local eateries:
Duke's Bakery Comfort Zone The Tipsy Toboggan The Old Grist Mill Tavern Gathering Grounds Cafe Canned Heat Craft Beer Pier 52 Mr. Chen Primo's on Water Street Sarcastic Sweets Green Jar Catering Red Oak Hospitality will be preparing a jumbo seafood paella throughout the afternoon for guests to enjoy.
What about drinks? Guests can also get a “coastal beer garden experience” by stopping on at the Oyster & Caviar Garden, where they’ll offer freshly shucked oysters and caviar service, as well as signature cocktails from Primo’s Bartending and craft beer brewed in Fall River.
How much is it to get into the Seafood Festival? Admission is $15 (with tickets available day-of) and includes access to a full lineup of unique eats.
Will there be entertainment? Festivities will feature live entertainment by DJ Dan Mac at the Fall River Carousel, as well as performances on the main stage in Heritage State Park by the Lainey Dionne Trio.
How do I get there and where do I park? Parking is available at Heritage State Park, with additional options along the Fall River waterfront. Or you can hop aboard the Fall River Water Taxi and arrive at the festival in style.
This article originally appeared on The Herald News: Great food and summer vibes at Fall River Seafood Festival
